assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production opaque 2D side-view game stage background for CPS Kitchen Catch, DAY CAFE / Normal difficulty. Input 1 is the existing kitchen: preserve its polished hand-painted pixel-cartoony rendering, honey wooden foreground counter dimensions and running-plane height, warm cocoa outlines and soft matte texture, NOT its kitchen layout. Inputs 2 and 3 are environment/mood references: cozy window light, quiet reading-cafe furniture and books. Create ONE wide 16:9 background, preferably 1920x1080, edge-to-edge with no borders. A cozy small cafe in golden daytime light: tall wooden window at far left; outside soft green foliage; pale warm cream central wall, restrained wooden wall trim; cafe bookshelf and a small upholstered chair confined to far right; a tiny cafe side table in the rear right with no food. A simple small upper-right shelf and discreet ceiling attachment points can accept separate hanging decorations later. Composition is a flat side-on game stage, not a perspective floor scene. Keep the central 65 percent of the upper playfield quiet, pale and largely empty for falling food; no focal furniture, signs, patterns, shelves, lamps or decorations in this central space. The foreground counter spans the entire bottom width. Its perfectly straight horizontal BACK/TOP EDGE is EXACTLY 78 percent down the image, with bright honey tabletop from y78 to y89 percent and wooden front fascia below y89, closely matching input 1's plane. This counter must stay empty and uninterrupted: no objects on the foreground playing surface, no table legs protruding above it, no floor slope. Moderately subdued background contrast so outlined game sprites read in front. Daylight is warm golden, fresh and welcoming, not blown out. No baked moving props: NO curtains, hanging plants, pendant lamps, steam, particles, falling objects, loose leaves or moving shadows with hard edges. Those will be separate overlays. No characters, mascot, food, trash, HUD, UI, text, lettering, logo, watermark, split panels or comparison sheet. Original cafe artwork that belongs to the same warm illustrated game world as the kitchen. Deliver only the background.

Use case: lighting-weather edit. Asset type: production opaque 2D game background, NIGHT CAFE / Hard difficulty, alternate time of day of the supplied DAY CAFE. Input 1 is the edit target. Keep EXACTLY the same room, viewpoint, crop, image dimensions, furniture, bookshelf, tiny table, chair, window geometry, hooks, wall trim, plant placement, hand-painted pixel-cartoony style and all foreground counter contours. Change ONLY time-of-day lighting and the exterior visible through the window. Make this cafe clearly night: deep desaturated blue-violet evening visible outside the left window, calm cool moonlight on the left side, rich cocoa wood shadows. Replace the bright yellow sunbeam and sharp daytime leaf shadows with softer subdued night illumination. Add cozy dim amber illumination from warm cafe lamps just OUTSIDE the upper-right crop: an inviting warm wash along the right wall/bookcase and counter, enough to suggest practical lamplight without adding visible light fixtures or changing any objects. The central wall must remain readable medium-value warm taupe, NOT black or high-contrast; this is a game stage behind colorful falling food. Countertop remains lit enough to see the player feet and its entire running edge. Preserve its perfectly straight top edge at y78 percent and its top-surface/fascia transition at y89 percent IDENTICALLY to the source. Central 65 percent stays quiet negative space. No neon, saturated purple lighting, horror atmosphere, excessive bloom, spotlight circles, vignette, people, food, mascot, trash, UI, labels, text, watermarks or particle effects. Do not add curtains, hanging plants, lamps, steam or rain streaks; moving decorations will be separate transparent sprites. Deliver a single full-width 16:9 night counterpart, no comparison panels. The difference should be genuine time-of-day lighting, not merely a uniform blue tint.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent 2D Unity ambient prop SPRITE ATLAS for the supplied Kitchen Catch cafe backgrounds. Input 1 is DAY CAFE style reference, input 2 is NIGHT CAFE lighting/material reference, NOT edit targets. Create exactly six isolated decorative prop sprites arranged in a clean THREE-COLUMN by TWO-ROW grid, one centered object per cell, generous transparent gutters and at least 10 percent transparent padding in every cell. One PNG with GENUINE alpha transparency; no drawn checkerboard or solid backdrop. The atlas is about 1536x1024, each cell square. Read order left to right: TOP LEFT one ivory linen cafe curtain panel tied back on one side, small honey wooden hanging bar, soft hem, entire panel visible, ready for subtle sway; TOP MIDDLE one antique brass cafe pendant lamp with short straight dark cord and softly amber bulb, front-facing, full cord and shade visible, lamp ends well within its cell, no outer glow or cast-light rectangle; TOP RIGHT one sage-green trailing ivy plant in a small terracotta hanging pot with two short suspension strings, whole object visible, not tangled, suitable for gentle sway. BOTTOM LEFT one small cream ceramic coffee cup on a matching saucer, warm brown coffee surface, no steam; BOTTOM MIDDLE one small upright fern in a simple pale ceramic pot; BOTTOM RIGHT one short stack of three closed muted sage/cocoa/cream cookbooks, no readable text or symbols on covers or spines. Original hand-painted pixel-cartoony game-art style matching the references: cocoa stepped outlines, warm wood/brass, creamy highlights, muted green leaves, restrained brushwork, orthographic front/side elevation, NOT photorealistic or 3D. Neutral warm material lighting usable in both scenes, shaded enough for volume but not highly glossy. These are scenery props, lower contrast than collectible food. Objects never touch, overlap or cross their cell boundaries. No scenery, background, wall, tabletop, floor, characters, food items, trash, logo, labels, gridlines, drop-shadow platform, detached fragments, steam, particles, checkerboard or watermark. Deliver only the six clean sprite cutouts in their transparent atlas.
